pricing_unit.model: Outcome-based pricing per resolution, with action credits or flex credits
pricing_unit.summary: The buyer pays for completed work, so variable spend follows volume and the seller must cap it with a commitment.

core_competitive_threats: BPO incumbents who already run the work
Pilot fatigue after repeated automation failures
cluster_objections: What happens to our per-resolution bill during peak traffic, and how do you guarantee the agent won't hallucinate a discount?
We have been burned by three automation pilots. Why is this one different?

cards.title: Where it sits
cards.body: Vertical and autonomous agents do a specific job end to end, such as claims or support.

cards.title: What the customer pays for
cards.body: Outcome-based pricing per resolution, with action credits or flex credits.

cards.title: How the money works
cards.body: Pricing per outcome means the vendor carries the accuracy risk, so the metric must be agreed up front.

cards.title: What threatens the deal
cards.body: BPO incumbents who already run the work, and pilot fatigue after failed automation.

quiz.prompt: What does a vertical agent buyer pay for?
quiz.why: The price follows each resolved outcome.

quiz.prompt: Who carries accuracy risk in outcome pricing?
quiz.why: If the agent fails, the vendor does not get paid for that outcome.

quiz.prompt: Which threat comes from past failures?
quiz.why: Buyers burned by earlier automation demand bounded proof.
